subject.title: Config: scaffold compaction loop guard settings

question: Should OpenClaw accept a reserved no-op `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` config surface now, or wait until the canonical saturated-session and compaction-rate-limit guard designs choose the final runtime-backed API?
rationale: This PR adds public config/default semantics without runtime behavior, while the linked design issues still need maintainer decisions about namespace, thresholds, validator behavior, and reset/throttle policy.

options.title: Resolve the guard contract first
options.body: Keep this PR open or ask for a rework until maintainers choose the permanent runtime-backed config/API shape in the canonical design thread.

options.title: Accept the scaffold deliberately
options.body: Merge the reserved config surface only if maintainers explicitly want to lock this namespace before detector/runtime work lands.

options.title: Close and replace later
options.body: Close this branch as superseded by the design issue and invite a fresh PR once the runtime guard contract is approved.

recommendation.title: Resolve the guard contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open or ask for a rework until maintainers choose the permanent runtime-backed config/API shape in the canonical design thread.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is adjacent safeguard compaction/default work plus the existing canonical issue review naming this handle for the config/product-shape decision.
